# OBJECTIVE
This document reports on the **community analyses** of the combined R1 experiment performed in the Fall of 2023 (completed Dec 2023) and R2 experiment performed in the Spring of 2024 (completed June 2024). Data represents the output of Miseq (R1) and NextSeq (R2) sequencing run of the Tri5 Mutant Microbiome project (Guixia Hao & Briana K. Whitaker & Nick Rhoades). 

# NOTES
* Changed chamber names for final figures from H/Howard = C1 and J/Josie = C2
* Removed outliers identified in Shannon Diveristy models from Structure models and PCoA figures: r1b "B-J-T5-1-11"; r2b "J-Tri5-05-R2-B"; r1f "F-J-Twn-4" and "F-H-Twn-6". Removal of the outliers had no effect on the p-values/Fstats (H-diversity or structure), but did improve model fit for the Shannon Diversity models.

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='hide', include=FALSE} 
x<-c("ggplot2", "phyloseq", "dplyr", "RColorBrewer", "DESeq2", "vegan", "RRPP",
     "ggVennDiagram", "viridis", "MASS", "car", "Biostrings", "egg", 
     "BiodiversityR", "tidyr")
lapply(x, require, character.only = TRUE)

#set seed
set.seed(128)

#Load functions
source("./code/multiplot.function.R")
`%nin%` = Negate(`%in%`)
gm_mean_protected <- function(x) {
  if (all(x == 0)) {
    return (0)
  }
  exp(mean(log(x[x != 0])))
}
# function for PCoA ellipses - 
veganCovEllipse <- function (cov, center = c(0, 0), scale = 1, npoints = 100)   {
  theta <- (0:npoints) * 2 * pi/npoints
  Circle <- cbind(cos(theta), sin(theta))
  t(center + scale * t(Circle %*% chol(cov)))    }

# set ggplot2 theme
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size=12)) 
theme_update(panel.grid.major=element_line(0), panel.grid.minor=element_line(0))

strain_col <- c("#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#1B9E77") #brewer.pal(3, name = "Dark2")

```

# Basic Taxa Info
```{r}
## Total Depth
depth_r1b <- sum(colSums(otu_table(ps_r1b))); depth_r1b
depth_r1f <- sum(colSums(otu_table(ps_r1f))); depth_r1f
depth_r2b <- sum(colSums(otu_table(ps_r2b))); depth_r2b
depth_r2f <- sum(colSums(otu_table(ps_r2f))); depth_r2f

# Top 10 Taxa
topten_r1b <- sort(colSums(otu_table(ps_r1b)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
tax_table(ps_r1b)[names(topten_r1b),c("family", "genus")]

topten_r1f <- sort(colSums(otu_table(ps_r1f)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
tax_table(ps_r1f)[names(topten_r1f),c("genus")]

topten_r2b <- sort(colSums(otu_table(ps_r2b)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
tax_table(ps_r2b)[names(topten_r2b),c("order", "family", "genus")]

topten_r2f <- sort(colSums(otu_table(ps_r2f)), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
tax_table(ps_r2f)[names(topten_r2f),c("phylum", "family", "genus")]

# Top 10 Taxa - proportion of reads
sum(topten_r1b/depth_r1b) 
sum(topten_r1f/depth_r1f) 
sum(topten_r2b/depth_r2b) 
sum(topten_r2f/depth_r2f) 

```

* The proportion of all read counts that the top 10 taxa in each round-kingdom contain indicates a highly biased community, with unequal colonization.

# Venn Diagram
```{r, echo = FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.height = 4, fig.width = 6}
### shared between Rounds
# Bacteria
r1b_ASVs <- colnames(ps_r1b@otu_table[,colSums(ps_r1b@otu_table) > 0])
r2b_ASVs <- colnames(ps_r2b@otu_table[,colSums(ps_r2b@otu_table) > 0])
mySet_b <- list(R1 = r1b_ASVs, R2 = r2b_ASVs) 
vd_b <- ggVennDiagram(mySet_b, label = "count", col = "gray", label_alpha = 0, label_size = 4) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1) +
    guides(fill = 'none') +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(rep("black",2))) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = .2)) +

```

* Only 16 Bacteria shared in common across all 4 Round-Chamber combinations, and only 5 Fungi.
* stronger overlap between chambers within Rounds, then between rounds

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = 'hide', fig.height = 5, fig.width = 9}
    Other = rowSums(decostand((otu_table(ps_r2b)),"total")[,other_r2b] ))
dat2_r2b <- reshape2::melt(dat_r2b, id.vars=c("Chamber.Rep", "Strain", "Strain_Chamber")) 
strain_r2b <- dat2_r2b %>% group_by(Strain_Chamber, variable) %>% summarize(value = sum(value))
plot_r2b <- ggplot(strain_r2b, aes(x = Strain_Chamber, y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = 'fill') +
  scale_fill_manual("ASV", values = asv_color_r2b) +
  xlab("") + ylab("Relative Abundance") +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

toptenNames_r2f <- names(topten_r2f)
other_r2f <- c(colnames(otu_table(ps_r2f))[colnames(otu_table(ps_r2f)) %nin% toptenNames_r2f])
dat_r2f <- data.frame(SbyE_r2f[,c("Chamber.Rep", "Strain", "Strain_Chamber")] ,
    decostand((otu_table(ps_r2f)),"total")[,toptenNames_r2f] ,
    Other = rowSums(decostand((otu_table(ps_r2f)),"total")[,other_r2f] ))
dat2_r2f <- reshape2::melt(dat_r2f, id.vars=c("Chamber.Rep", "Strain", "Strain_Chamber")) 
strain_r2f <- dat2_r2f %>% group_by(Strain_Chamber, variable) %>% summarize(value = sum(value))
plot_r2f <- ggplot(strain_r2f, aes(x = Strain_Chamber, y = value, fill = variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = 'fill') +
  scale_fill_manual("ASV", values = asv_color_r2f) +
  xlab("") + ylab("Relative Abundance") +
  theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
#tiff("./figures/RelAbun_Rounds.tiff", width=24, height=16, units="cm", res=300)
multiplot(plot_r1b, plot_r1f, plot_r2b, plot_r2f, cols = 2)
#dev.off()

```
* Fungi - clear dominance of Fusarium in Fusarium treaetments in both rounds. Highest distribution of diversity in the control treatments. But otherwise, more similarities between Fusarium treatments (PH1 and Tri5 mutant) and betweeen chambers, then is seen for bacteria overall.
* Bacteria - Dominance of ASV1-Erwiniaceae in Round 1 as well as in several chambers in Round 2. in Round 1 - moderate differences between chambers and between treatments. Stronger chamber and treatment differences in Round 2, with less cohernence in what is actually going on.

### Shannon Diversity
```{r, fig.keep = 'none'}
# par(mfrow = c(2,2))
# par(mfrow = c(1,1))

div_r1b <- lm((Hdiv) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep,
              data = SbyE_r1b[SbyE_r1b$Sample_ID != "B-J-T5-1-11",])
#plot(div_r1b)           #when sqrt used, its good
#car::boxCox(div_r1b, lambda = seq(0, 1, 0.1))  # about 0.3,
div_r1b_a <- lm( I(((Hdiv^0.3)-1)/0.3) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r1b[SbyE_r1b$Sample_ID != "B-J-T5-1-11",])
#plot(div_r1b_a)           #good
Anova(div_r1b_a, type = 3)
summary(div_r1b_a)$adj.r.squared


div_r1f <- lm(log(Hdiv+0.01) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r1f[SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-J-Twn-4" &   #has 0 for hdiv
                              SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-H-Twn-6" ,]) #lowest hdiv in its group by a lot
#plot(div_r1f)           #when those 2 samples are removed, this is ok
Anova(div_r1f, type = 3) #strain signif
summary(div_r1f)$adj.r.squared
div_r1f_a <- lm(I(Hdiv+0.01) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r1f[SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-J-Twn-4" &   #has 0 for hdiv
                              SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-H-Twn-6" ,])
#car::boxCox(div_r1f_a, lambda = seq(-0.5, 0.5, 0.1))  #really close to 0, 
                                  # so log is the best transformation


div_r2b <- lm((Hdiv) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep,
              data = SbyE_r2b[SbyE_r2b$Sample_ID !="J-Tri5-05-R2-B",])
#plot(div_r2b)           #when sqrt is ok/good -
                        #NOTE -different outlier than richness models
#car::boxCox(div_r2b, lambda = seq(0, 1, 0.1))  # about 0.5
div_r2b_a <- lm(I(((Hdiv^0.5)-1)/0.5) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r2b[SbyE_r2b$Sample_ID !="J-Tri5-05-R2-B",])
#plot(div_r2b_a)           #good
Anova(div_r2b_a, type = 3)
summary(div_r2b_a)$adj.r.squared


div_r2f <- lm((Hdiv) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, data = SbyE_r2f)
#plot(div_r2f)             # bad :/ either sqrt or log
     # ph1 and tri5 treatments break homoscedasticity, even with transformations
#car::boxCox(div_r2f, lambda = seq(0, 1, 0.1))   # about 0.4, large 95% CI range
div_r2f_a <- lm(I(((Hdiv^0.4)-1)/0.4) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, data = SbyE_r2f)
#plot(div_r2f_a)           #bad, but maybe slightly better than reg. transformations
Anova(div_r2f_a, type = 3)  # but again, signif strain makes sense w/ figure
summary(div_r2f_a)$adj.r.squared


# note, for r2f, 3 samples driving outliers in residuals figures, all from J-Tri5 treatment, but no good reason to remove them, and they are in the range with chamber H and the PH1 treatment. Unlike with r1f where the two outliers were clearly very distinctive within their respective chambers
```

#### posthocs
```{r}
# change models to aov
div_r1b_aov <- aov( I(((Hdiv^0.3)-1)/0.3) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r1b[SbyE_r1b$Sample_ID != "B-J-T5-1-11",])
div_r1f_aov <- aov(log(Hdiv+0.01) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r1f[SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-J-Twn-4" &
                              SbyE_r1f$Sample_ID != "F-H-Twn-6" ,])
div_r2b_aov <- aov(I(((Hdiv^0.5)-1)/0.5) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, 
              data = SbyE_r2b[SbyE_r2b$Sample_ID !="J-Tri5-05-R2-B",])
div_r2f_aov <- aov(I(((Hdiv^0.4)-1)/0.4) ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, data = SbyE_r2f)

# Fungi - only test Strain main effect
TukeyHSD(div_r1f_aov, which = "Strain")
TukeyHSD(div_r2f_aov, which = "Strain")
# clear result - fungal diversity in control treatments consistently higher

# Bacteria
TukeyHSD(div_r1b_aov, which = "Strain") #ph1 higher div than tri5 or cont
TukeyHSD(div_r2b_aov, which = "Strain") #NS

TukeyHSD(div_r1b_aov, which = "Chamber.Rep") #C2 higher div
TukeyHSD(div_r2b_aov, which = "Chamber.Rep") #NS

TukeyHSD(div_r1b_aov, which = "Strain:Chamber.Rep")
TukeyHSD(div_r2b_aov, which = "Strain:Chamber.Rep")

```
* fungal result clear -- fungal diversity in control treatments consistently higher
* bacterial results more muddled

# Structure
* adonis2 and RRPP agree with one another, but RRPP output provides F-statistics and p-values for all model terms
```{r}
# r1b
comm_r1b <- adonis2(VST2_r1b ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep,
                    perm=199, method = "euclidean", data=SbyE2_r1b,
                    binary = FALSE, by = "margin" )
comm_r1b 
rrpp_r1b <- lm.rrpp(dist2_r1b ~ Strain * Chamber.Rep, iter = 999,
                    print.progress = FALSE, data = SbyE2_r1b, SS.type="III")
anova(rrpp_r1b, effect.type = "F")
```

### Unusual Pattern in R2-Fungi PCoA
```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=4}
#pcoa_noFus_r2f

# calculate relative abundance of each species wi/in sites
REL_noFus_r2f <- VST_noFus_r2f #where fish is species mat w/ sites as rows
for(i in 1:nrow(VST_noFus_r2f)) {
    REL_noFus_r2f[i, ] = VST_noFus_r2f[i, ] / sum(VST_noFus_r2f[i, ]) 
    }
#calculate the species-scores/explanatory-vectors using results of the whole PCoA
pcoa_noFus_r2f <- add.spec.scores(pcoa_noFus_r2f, REL_noFus_r2f, method = "pcoa.scores")


#define the 'important' species based on a threshold
corr_noFus_r2f <- add.spec.scores(pcoa_noFus_r2f, REL_noFus_r2f, method = "cor.scores")$cproj 

#save only the important species 
corrcut <- 0.7 # define a correlational cutoff
imp_noFus_r2f <- 
    corr_noFus_r2f[abs(corr_noFus_r2f[, 1]) >= corrcut | abs(corr_noFus_r2f[, 2]) >= corrcut, ] 
#imp_noFus_r2f
imp_nam_noFus_r2f <- rownames(imp_noFus_r2f)
ps_r2f@tax_table[imp_nam_noFus_r2f,c('phylum','genus')]
pcoa_noFus_r2f$cproj[imp_nam_noFus_r2f, ]*10000

test <- data.frame(corr_noFus_r2f[imp_nam_noFus_r2f, ])
test$ids <- rownames(test)

pc4_specScores <- ggplot() + #coord_equal() + 
    geom_path(data = ell_noFus_SxC_r2f, aes(x = V1, y = V2,
          group = StrainChamber, colour = Strain, linetype = Chamber.Rep), linewidth = 1.1,
          show.legend = TRUE) +
    geom_point(data = pdat_noFus_r2f, aes(x = V1, y = V2, 
          color = Strain, shape = Chamber.Rep) , size = 2) +
    geom_text(data = test, 
               aes(x = Dim1*10, y = Dim2*10, label = ids), size =3)+
    scale_color_manual(values = c(brewer.pal(3, name = "Dark2"))) +
    scale_linetype_manual("Chamber", values = c(1,2)) +
    scale_shape_manual("Chamber", values = c(16,15))

#tiff("./figures/PCoA_r2f_specScores.tiff", width=6, height=5, units="in", res=300)
pc4_specScores
#dev.off()
```

* of the taxa significantly correlated with an axes, both ASV6 and ASV141 fall closer to the odd points along V1 axis and have a distinctive patterns of either 0 or high rel. abundance in half the samples pretty evenly split across treatments (not shown, box plots of relative abundance)

# Disease Models
```{r, results = 'hide', echo =  FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 6}
SbyE_r1b %>% 
    dplyr::select(Strain, Chamber.Rep, Strain_Chamber, FgTa_ratio, ugDON_per_g) %>% 
    mutate("Round" = "R1") -> out1
SbyE_r2b %>% 
    dplyr::select(Strain, Chamber.Rep, Strain_Chamber, FgTa_ratio, ugDON_per_g) %>% 
    mutate("Round" = "R2") %>% rbind(., out1) -> dat
dat %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(FgTa_ratio, ugDON_per_g)) -> dat2

dis_plot <- ggplot(dat2, aes(x = Chamber.Rep, y = value, color = Strain, group = Strain_Chamber)) +
    facet_grid(name ~ Round, scales = "free_y") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15)) +
    scale_color_manual("Strain", values = strain_col) +
    scale_x_discrete('Chamber') + scale_y_continuous("") +
    theme(legend.position = 'inside', legend.position.inside = c(0.1, 0.88), 
          legend.background = element_blank())

#tiff("./figures/Disease_figure.tiff", width=6, height=5.5, units="in", res=300)
dis_plot
#dev.off()
```

```{r}
#hist(log(dat$ugDON_per_g), breaks = 10)
#hist(log(dat$FgTa_ratio), breaks = 10)
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
fgr <- lm(log(FgTa_ratio+0.5) ~ Strain*Chamber.Rep*Round, data = dat[dat$Strain != "Cont",])
#plot(fgr)  #H-PH1-06-R2 is an outlier
Anova(fgr, type = 3)

don <- lm(log(ugDON_per_g+1) ~ Chamber.Rep*Round, data = dat[dat$Strain == "PH1",])
#plot(don)  #H-PH1-06-R2 is an outlier here also
Anova(don, type = 3)

#SbyE_r2b[SbyE_r2b$Sample_ID == "H-PH1-06-R2-B",] 

```
* disease models - NOTE - "H-PH1-06-R2-B is an outlier in both, and has lowest DON and FgTa by a lot, but does not match the diversity model outliers & no big incentive to remove
